body: Three legs, all required: (1) Business - extraordinary economics, measured by high, durable returns on owners' capital (ROE/ROIC) without heavy leverage; (2) People - skilled, honest management that treats shareholders as partners and has a record of good capital allocation; (3) Reinvestment - the ability to reinvest free cash flow at similar high returns for many years (runway). When a 'compounding machine' is found, the default is to hold; turnover is very low and selling happens when a leg breaks (reinvestment runway ends, management changes behaviour), not on valuation alone. Indian checklist translation: ROCE >20% for 7-10 years, low debt, promoters with clean related-party and pledge history, capex funded internally with incremental ROCE staying high, and a TAM that supports a decade of growth. Risk: paying any price for quality (de-rating), and confusing a cyclical peak ROE for a durable one.
title: Akre: three-legged stool compounding machines
